title: GMAO SaaS Platform
description: Industrial maintenance management system built for multi-tenant scale — technicians, machines, and inventory in one API.
caseStudy:
Managing industrial maintenance means coordinating technicians, machine state, and inventory. Existing tools were either too slow or too painful to plug into a modern web stack.

I architected a modular SaaS backend with **FastAPI** and **PostgreSQL**, role-based access, and maintenance scheduling workflows. The whole stack is containerized so deployments stay boring — the good kind of boring.

```python
# tenants stay isolated; workflows stay explicit
async def schedule_work_order(tenant_id: str, asset_id: str) -> WorkOrder:
    return await work_orders.create(tenant_id, asset_id)
```

**Role:** Full Stack / Backend Engineer.
**Lesson:** multi-tenant data models fail first at the edges — permissions and migrations — not at the happy path.

title: Document Processing RAG Pipeline
description: Asynchronous document ingestion and retrieval-augmented generation. PDFs go in; grounded answers come out.
caseStudy:
Dumping huge PDFs into an LLM context window is a great way to hit timeouts, lose pages, and retrieve the wrong paragraph.

I designed a fault-tolerant ingestion pipeline: **Temporal** orchestrates chunking, embedding, and storage; **Kafka** moves work between services; **LangChain** handles semantic chunking before vectors land in the DB.

```ts
const pipeline = {
  ingest: 'temporal-workflow',
  queue: 'kafka',
  retrieve: 'vector-search + rerank',
};
```

**Role:** Backend Engineer.
**Lesson:** RAG quality is mostly data plumbing. Fancy prompts cannot save a bad chunker.

title: SCADA Data Connector
description: Real-time telemetry aggregation for industrial PLCs — the bridge between shop-floor hardware and web dashboards.
caseStudy:
Legacy industrial equipment does not speak React. This connector aggregates high-throughput sensor data with **Redis streams** and **Kafka**, then hands a clean feed to modern dashboards.

Fault-tolerance and automatic reconnection were non-negotiable: a dropped PLC should not take the rest of the plant view with it.

**Role:** Systems Engineer.
**Lesson:** retries without backoff are just a DDoS against your own hardware.

title: ft_transcendence
description: Real-time multiplayer Pong with chat, OAuth2, and 2FA. Yes, Pong. No, it was not simple.
caseStudy:
A complete SPA: **NestJS** backend, **Vue.js** frontend, WebSocket gameplay and chat, OAuth2 + 2FA, all wrapped in Docker.

The hard part was not drawing a rectangle. It was keeping game state honest when two clients and a chat thread all think they are the source of truth.

**Lesson:** realtime systems fail in the 50ms you did not budget for.

title: This Portfolio (Night Owl Edition)
description: A portfolio that pretends to be VS Code. Projects and posts are JSON files. The theme is the one I actually work in.
caseStudy:
I spend most of my waking hours in an editor. A corporate landing page felt like wearing someone else's hoodie.

This site is a themed workspace: explorer, tabs, status bar, command palette (`Ctrl/Cmd+K`), and a terminal (`Ctrl+``). Content lives in `src/data/*.json` so I never have to hunt through JSX to add a project.

```json
{ "id": "developer-portfolio", "status": "live", "featured": true }
```

**Lesson:** if updating the site hurts, you will not update the site.

title: Dining Philosophers
description: Five guys, five forks, zero starvation. I made them behave.
caseStudy:
Classic deadlock playground. One mutex was not enough, so I invented a waiter.

They eat forever now. No drama. Click the repo if you want to watch them choke first.

**Lesson:** starvation is a product bug, even when the product is five imaginary philosophers.

title: Docker Inception
description: Six containers in one box: WordPress thinks it is alone, Redis thinks it is the boss.
caseStudy:
A Compose stack where everything talks and nobody crashes. WordPress, Redis, Nginx, MariaDB, FTPS, Adminer — one `make up` and it just… works.

The Compose file is tiny. Feels like cheating. It is not.

**Lesson:** if you cannot explain the network graph on a napkin, you do not own the stack.

title: STL from Scratch
description: Map, vector, stack — I wrote them. GCC cried.
caseStudy:
No stolen templates. All original pain. Allocators, iterators, and the quiet horror of `map`.

Faster insert? Sometimes. Memory leak? Nope.

**Lesson:** you do not understand a container until you have implemented `rebalance` at 2am.

title: MiniShell
description: A shell that survives `cat | wc | grep`. My cat survived too.
caseStudy:
Pipes, quotes, job control — a small Bourne-ish shell. `SIGINT` works. `SIGTSTP` too. No segfaults on the paths I actually test (yes, I hear you).

Try: `ping example.com &` then try to kill me.

**Lesson:** shells are just process trees with opinions.

title: FT-WebServer
description: Built Nginx-adjacent HTTP in C++. Served hundreds of simulated users. Zero leaks. I went to sleep.
caseStudy:
Event loop. No threads. Then siege. It laughed. Then it answered.

Non-blocking I/O is a lifestyle, not a flag.

**Lesson:** `epoll` will not save you from forgetting to close a socket.
